=== Medici: Sealed Harbour ===

Three Florentine merchants in seats 1, 2 and 3. Each starts with 25 florins; florin totals are public.

The deck has 20 cards: one of each combination of 4 commodities (Grain, Cloth, Spice, Dye) and values 1 to 5. At the start of the game, 3 of the 4 commodities are dealt at random, one to each player, as that player's secret patron commodity. Each player sees only their own. The fourth commodity is nobody's patron.

The game has 3 days of 6 rounds each, 18 rounds in all. At the start of each day the full deck is shuffled and every ship is empty. Each ship holds at most 3 cards per day; a full ship can take no more cards that day. Day 1 begins with seat 1 as seller, day 2 with seat 2, day 3 with seat 3, and the seller then moves to the next seat each round (1, 2, 3, 1, ...), so each player sells exactly 2 times per day.

EACH ROUND
1. Draw: the top card of the deck is revealed to everyone. This card is the lot.
2. Talk: all three players write one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Talk is not binding.
3. Reserve: the seller secretly chooses a reserve price, a whole number from 1 to 6.
4. Bids: at the same moment, the two non-sellers each choose a sealed bid, a whole number from 0 to 10, no more than their current florins. A bid of 0 means pass. A player whose ship already holds 3 cards must bid 0 (they are not asked; their bid is 0), as is a player with no florins.
5. Resolve, case A (a bid reaches the reserve): the highest bid wins. If the two bids tie, the bidder sitting first clockwise after the seller wins. The winner pays their bid to the seller and loads the card.
6. Resolve, case B (no bid reaches the reserve): if the seller's ship has room, the seller must load the card and pay the reserve to the bank. If the seller's ship is full, the card is discarded and no one pays. If the seller has fewer florins than the reserve, they pay all they have and still load the card if the ship has room.
7. Reveal: the reserve, both bids, the buyer and the price are announced to everyone.

END OF EACH DAY (after rounds 6, 12 and 18)
- Ship prize: each player's ship value is the sum of the card values in their ship. Highest ship value receives 12 florins and second highest receives 6. If two or more players tie, they add together the prizes for the places they occupy and split the sum equally, rounded down (two tied for first get 9 each; three tied get 6 each; two tied for second get 3 each). A player with an empty ship never receives a prize and occupies no place.
- Patron bonus: each player receives 3 florins for each card of their own patron commodity in their ship.
- Empty-slot penalty: each player pays the bank 2 florins for each empty slot in their ship (0 to 3 slots). Florins cannot drop below 0.
- Reset: ships are emptied and the next day begins.

After the end-of-day scoring of day 3, the player with the most florins wins. If two or three players tie for most, it is a draw between them and they share the win.

=== Medici: Sealed Harbour ===

Three Florentine merchants in seats 1, 2 and 3. Each starts with 25 florins; florin totals are public.

The deck has 20 cards: one of each combination of 4 commodities (Grain, Cloth, Spice, Dye) and values 1 to 5. At the start of the game, 3 of the 4 commodities are dealt at random, one to each player, as that player's secret patron commodity. Each player sees only their own. The fourth commodity is nobody's patron.

The game has 3 days of 6 rounds each, 18 rounds in all. At the start of each day the full deck is shuffled and every ship is empty. Each ship holds at most 3 cards per day; a full ship can take no more cards that day. Day 1 begins with seat 1 as seller, day 2 with seat 2, day 3 with seat 3, and the seller then moves to the next seat each round (1, 2, 3, 1, ...), so each player sells exactly 2 times per day.

EACH ROUND
1. Draw: the top card of the deck is revealed to everyone. This card is the lot.
2. Talk: all three players write one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Talk is not binding.
3. Reserve: the seller secretly chooses a reserve price, a whole number from 1 to 6.
4. Bids: at the same moment, the two non-sellers each choose a sealed bid, a whole number from 0 to 10, no more than their current florins. A bid of 0 means pass. A player whose ship already holds 3 cards must bid 0 (they are not asked; their bid is 0), as is a player with no florins.
5. Resolve, case A (a bid reaches the reserve): the highest bid wins. If the two bids tie, the bidder sitting first clockwise after the seller wins. The winner pays their bid to the seller and loads the card.
6. Resolve, case B (no bid reaches the reserve): if the seller's ship has room, the seller must load the card and pay the reserve to the bank. If the seller's ship is full, the card is discarded and no one pays. If the seller has fewer florins than the reserve, they pay all they have and still load the card if the ship has room.
7. Reveal: the reserve, both bids, the buyer and the price are announced to everyone.

- Ship prize: each player's ship value is the sum of the card values in their ship. Highest ship value receives 12 florins and second highest receives 6. If two or more players tie, they add together the prizes for the places they occupy and split the sum equally, rounded down (two tied for first get 9 each; three tied get 6 each; two tied for second get 3 each). EACH ROUND
1. Draw: the top card of the deck is revealed to everyone. This card is the lot.
2. Talk: all three players write one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Talk is not binding.
3. Reserve: the seller secretly chooses a reserve price, a whole number from 1 to 6.
4. Bids: at the same moment, the two non-sellers each choose a sealed bid, a whole number from 0 to 10, no more than their current florins. A bid of 0 means pass. A player whose ship already holds 3 cards must bid 0 (they are not asked; their bid is 0), as is a player with no florins.

=== Medici: Sealed Harbour ===

Three Florentine merchants in seats 1, 2 and 3. Each starts with 25 florins; florin totals are public.

The deck has 20 cards: one of each combination of 4 commodities (Grain, Cloth, Spice, Dye) and values 1 to 5. At the start of the game, 3 of the 4 commodities are dealt at random, one to each player, as that player's secret patron commodity. Each player sees only their own. The fourth commodity is nobody's patron.

The game has 3 days of 6 rounds each, 18 rounds in all. At the start of each day the full deck is shuffled and every ship is empty. Each ship holds at most 3 cards per day; a full ship can take no more cards that day. Day 1 begins with seat 1 as seller, day 2 with seat 2, day 3 with seat 3, and the seller then moves to the next seat each round (1, 2, 3, 1, ...), so each player sells exactly 2 times per day.

EACH ROUND
1. Draw: the top card of the deck is revealed to everyone. This card is the lot.
2. Talk: all three players write one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Talk is not binding.
3. Reserve: the seller secretly chooses a reserve price, a whole number from 1 to 6.
4. Bids: at the same moment, the two non-sellers each choose a sealed bid, a whole number from 0 to 10, no more than their current florins. A bid of 0 means pass. A player whose ship already holds 3 cards must bid 0 (they are not asked; their bid is 0), as is a player with no florins.
5. Resolve, case A (a bid reaches the reserve): the highest bid wins. If the two bids tie, the bidder sitting first clockwise after the seller wins. The winner pays their bid to the seller and loads the card.
6. Resolve, case B (no bid reaches the reserve): if the seller's ship has room, the seller must load the card and pay the reserve to the bank. If the seller's ship is full, the card is discarded and no one pays. If the seller has fewer florins than the reserve, they pay all they have and still load the card if the ship has room.
7. Reveal: the reserve, both bids, the buyer and the price are announced to everyone.

END OF EACH DAY (after rounds 6, 12 and 18)
- Ship prize: each player's ship value is the sum of the card values in their ship. Highest ship value receives 12 florins and second highest receives 6. If two or more players tie, they add together the prizes for the places they occupy and split the sum equally, rounded down (two tied for first get 9 each; three tied get 6 each; two tied for second get 3 each). A player with an empty ship never receives a prize and occupies no place.
- Patron bonus: each player receives 3 florins for each card of their own patron commodity in their ship.
- Empty-slot penalty: each player pays the bank 2 florins for each empty slot in their ship (0 to 3 slots). Florins cannot drop below 0.
- Reset: ships are emptied and the next day begins.

After the end-of-day scoring of day 3, the player with the most florins wins. If two or three players tie for most, it is a draw between them and they share the win.

=== Medici: Sealed Harbour ===

Three Florentine merchants in seats 1, 2 and 3. Each starts with 25 florins; florin totals are public.

The deck has 20 cards: one of each combination of 4 commodities (Grain, Cloth, Spice, Dye) and values 1 to 5. At the start of the game, 3 of the 4 commodities are dealt at random, one to each player, as that player's secret patron commodity. Each player sees only their own. The fourth commodity is nobody's patron.

The game has 3 days of 6 rounds each, 18 rounds in all. At the start of each day the full deck is shuffled and every ship is empty. Each ship holds at most 3 cards per day; a full ship can take no more cards that day. Day 1 begins with seat 1 as seller, day 2 with seat 2, day 3 with seat 3, and the seller then moves to the next seat each round (1, 2, 3, 1, ...), so each player sells exactly 2 times per day.

EACH ROUND
1. Draw: the top card of the deck is revealed to everyone. This card is the lot.
2. Talk: all three players write one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Talk is not binding.
3. Reserve: the seller secretly chooses a reserve price, a whole number from 1 to 6.
4. Bids: at the same moment, the two non-sellers each choose a sealed bid, a whole number from 0 to 10, no more than their current florins. A bid of 0 means pass. A player whose ship already holds 3 cards must bid 0 (they are not asked; their bid is 0), as is a player with no florins.
5. Resolve, case A (a bid reaches the reserve): the highest bid wins. If the two bids tie, the bidder sitting first clockwise after the seller wins. The winner pays their bid to the seller and loads the card.
6. Resolve, case B (no bid reaches the reserve): if the seller's ship has room, the seller must load the card and pay the reserve to the bank. If the seller's ship is full, the card is discarded and no one pays. If the seller has fewer florins than the reserve, they pay all they have and still load the card if the ship has room.
7. Reveal: the reserve, both bids, the buyer and the price are announced to everyone.

END OF EACH DAY (after rounds 6, 12 and 18)
- Ship prize: each player's ship value is the sum of the card values in their ship. Highest ship value receives 12 florins and second highest receives 6. If two or more players tie, they add together the prizes for the places they occupy and split the sum equally, rounded down (two tied for first get 9 each; three tied get 6 each; two tied for second get 3 each). A player with an empty ship never receives a prize and occupies no place.
- Patron bonus: each player receives 3 florins for each card of their own patron commodity in their ship.

- Reset: ships are emptied and the next day begins.

After the end-of-day scoring of day 3, the player with the most florins wins. If two or three players tie for most, it is a draw between them and they share the win.

=== Medici: Sealed Harbour ===

Three Florentine merchants in seats 1, 2 and 3. Each starts with 25 florins; florin totals are public.

The deck has 20 cards: one of each combination of 4 commodities (Grain, Cloth, Spice, Dye) and values 1 to 5. At the start of the game, 3 of the 4 commodities are dealt at random, one to each player, as that player's secret patron commodity. Each player sees only their own. The fourth commodity is nobody's patron.

The game has 3 days of 6 rounds each, 18 rounds in all. At the start of each day the full deck is shuffled and every ship is empty. Each ship holds at most 3 cards per day; a full ship can take no more cards that day. Day 1 begins with seat 1 as seller, day 2 with seat 2, day 3 with seat 3, and the seller then moves to the next seat each round (1, 2, 3, 1, ...), so each player sells exactly 2 times per day.

EACH ROUND
1. Draw: the top card of the deck is revealed to everyone. This card is the lot.
2. Talk: all three players write one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Talk is not binding.
3. Reserve: the seller secretly chooses a reserve price, a whole number from 1 to 6.
4. Bids: at the same moment, the two non-sellers each choose a sealed bid, a whole number from 0 to 10, no more than their current florins. A bid of 0 means pass. A player whose ship already holds 3 cards must bid 0 (they are not asked; their bid is 0), as is a player with no florins.
5. Resolve, case A (a bid reaches the reserve): the highest bid wins. If the two bids tie, the bidder sitting first clockwise after the seller wins. The winner pays their bid to the seller and loads the card.
6. Resolve, case B (no bid reaches the reserve): if the seller's ship has room, the seller must load the card and pay the reserve to the bank. If the seller's ship is full, the card is discarded and no one pays. If the seller has fewer florins than the reserve, they pay all they have and still load the card if the ship has room.
7. Reveal: the reserve, both bids, the buyer and the price are announced to everyone.

END OF EACH DAY (after rounds 6, 12 and 18)
- Ship prize: each player's ship value is the sum of the card values in their ship. Highest ship value receives 12 florins and second highest receives 6. If two or more players tie, they add together the prizes for the places they occupy and split the sum equally, rounded down (two tied for first get 9 each; three tied get 6 each; two tied for second get 3 each). A player with an empty ship never receives a prize and occupies no place.
- Patron bonus: each player receives 3 florins for each card of their own patron commodity in their ship.
- Empty-slot penalty: each player pays the bank 2 florins for each empty slot in their ship (0 to 3 slots). Florins cannot drop below 0.
- Reset: ships are emptied and the next day begins.

After the end-of-day scoring of day 3, the player with the most florins wins. If two or three players tie for most, it is a draw between them and they share the win.

Day 1 begins with seat 1 as seller, day 2 with seat 2, day 3 with seat 3, and the seller then moves to the next seat each round (1, 2, 3, 1, ...), so each player sells exactly 2 times per day.

EACH ROUND
1. Draw: the top card of the deck is revealed to everyone. This card is the lot.
2. Talk: all three players write one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Talk is not binding.
3. Reserve: the seller secretly chooses a reserve price, a whole number from 1 to 6.
4. Bids: at the same moment, the two non-sellers each choose a sealed bid, a whole number from 0 to 10, no more than their current florins. A bid of 0 means pass. A player whose ship already holds 3 cards must bid 0 (they are not asked; their bid is 0), as is a player with no florins.

6. Resolve, case B (no bid reaches the reserve): if the seller's ship has room, the seller must load the card and pay the reserve to the bank.
